transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2025-10-28 15:30 PST
- Duration: ~72 minutes
- Recording: enabled

Summary/Topics (auto): egress segmentation; NAT vs proxy; firewall appliances; KMS BYOK and HSM attestations; audit log forwarding; RBAC/SSO integration; canary testing plan

00:00:03 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. Alex Mercer from Redwood inference, AE. With me are Samir, our solutions SE, and Lena. How's everyone doing?
00:00:12 Dana (NorthStar): Hi Alex, thanks. Dana here. We're excited to get into the network bits — Priya and Miguel are on for security and infra.
00:00:20 Priya (NorthStar): Morning, all. I wanted to make sure we nail down the egress posture; SOC 2 wants explicit egress controls and evidence that logs can't be tampered with.
00:00:28 Samir (Redwood): Yep, totally. High level: for Redwood Private we can support full VPC isolation, optional private control plane, and a BYOK flow using your KMS/HSM or Redwood-managed keys. Today I want to talk specifically about egress — options are NAT + NACLs/SGs, egress proxy in subnet, or inline firewall appliance like Palo Alto or a cloud FW.
00:00:45 Miguel (NorthStar): Quick ask — we prefer no open internet egress from inference nodes. Everything must go through approved proxies or be to whitelisted endpoints.
00:00:52 Samir (Redwood): That's fine. We typically recommend an explicit deny default, then allowlist outbound for: Redwood control plane (if you use hosted control plane endpoints), image registry access for updates, and telemetry endpoints if you opt into telemetry. For total air-gap, you can run with private control plane and local image registry.
00:01:14 Priya: And audit logs? We need immutable logs shipped to our Splunk instance with tamper-evident properties. CloudTrail + VPC Flow logs plus application-level logs. Can Redwood sign the logs or forward them?
00:01:25 Lena (Redwood): We can forward application audit events to your SIEM over TLS to a designated endpoint. For immutability, we recommend forwarding to an ingestion pipeline that writes to an append-only store; if you use Splunk we support HEC token ingestion and can also push CloudTrail from the cloud-side. For BYOK HSM attestation, we can record key usage events in the audit trail.
00:01:47 Dana: Walk us through the egress proxy option vs NAT. What's the operational tradeoff?
00:01:54 Samir: Sure — NAT gateway is simple: your nodes use a NAT and you control NACLs&SGs. Downside: coarse-grain, hard to do per-model or per-tenant egress policies. A forward proxy (squid/Envoy) lets you apply allowlists per route, embed mTLS, and do HTTP-level logging with rich metadata. Inline firewall appliance gives you advanced IDS/IPS features but adds complexity and stateful run concerns.
00:02:25 Miguel: If we do a proxy, does Redwood manage it or do we? We prefer infra ownership.
00:02:31 Samir: You can host the proxy in your VPC. Redwood supports proxy configuration via environment vars and route tables; our runtime can be pinned to use the proxy. For managed proxy, Redwood can run an HA pair inside your dedicated subnet under a managed contract.
00:02:45 Priya: For SOC 2 we need RBAC/SSO. How does Redwood integrate with Okta and SCIM?
00:02:51 Alex: We have SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to roles in the Console — you can map SAML attributes to roles, and we emit audit events for role changes. Also we have token-level access logs for inference calls.
00:03:05 Priya: Can those logs be exported to our SIEM w/out exposing secrets?
00:03:10 Lena: Yes, logs are exports only; secrets (API keys) are not exported. We can redact tokens and only include token hash and metadata for diagnostics.
00:03:20 Miguel: On-network specifics: we run private subnets for compute, a restricted mgmt subnet, and a logging VPC peered to Splunk ingest. We'll need IP ranges.
00:03:29 Samir: We'll give a recommended CIDR map for subnets and expected outbound IPs. If you use a managed NAT, outbound IPs are stable per AZ; for Redwoods hosted egress endpoints we publish a set of IPs you can allowlist.
00:03:44 Dana: What about egress to model registries and container registries during patch? Need to approve those domains/IPs.
00:03:50 Samir: Recommended approach: pre-pull images into a local registry during a maintenance window. For emergency patches we support signed artifacts you can host locally.
00:04:00 Priya: KMS — BYOK. We need HSM hardware security module with FIPS 140-2 level 3?
00:04:08 Lena: Redwood supports BYOK with customer-managed KMS. For cloud customers we support AWS KMS with key policies and CloudHSM for attestation. For on-prem HSMs you can bring an HSM that supports PKCS#11; we have a connector. Key operations are logged and we can include key usage events in the audit stream.
00:04:26 Miguel: Rotation? Who rotates? Can keys be rotated without restarting running containers?
00:04:31 Samir: Short answer: yes, most keys can be rotated with a rolling rekey process. We use envelope encryption: data keys are inside the node and wrapped by KMS. Rotation of the wrapping key doesn't require stopping inference, we rewrap new data keys as they roll. For legacy cases we can schedule a rolling restart during maintenance windows.
00:04:50 Priya: About tamper-evident logs: can Redwood write signed log bundles?
00:04:55 Lena: We sign log batches w/ a service key and include signatures in the payload. Alternatively we push directly to your Splunk HEC over mTLS and you can configure your ingestion to verify certificates. Either way we can provide chain-of-custody artifacts for SOC auditors.
00:05:12 Dana: Any concern about data residency? Some PHI must stay in-region.
00:05:18 Alex: We can pin deployment to specific region endpoints, including private deployments on-prem. If you're doing hybrid we can ensure model weights and request data never leave the designated region, and we can disable any cross-region fallback.
00:05:30 Miguel: Firewalling — do you require any inbound ports? We want to minimize attack surface.
00:05:36 Samir: Inbound is minimal: management plane (control plane) connections can be via private link or VPN — if you pick private control plane there's no public inbound to compute nodes. For optional inbound (debugging), it's tunneled over a mTLS connection from a known management jump host with strict RBAC.
00:05:56 Priya: How do we prove the control plane can't access customer data?
00:06:00 Lena: We can provide architecture diagrams plus attestations. Data plane for inference executes only on your compute nodes; logs we forward per your policy. The control plane stores metadata, not payloads, unless you opt into telemetry. We can disable telemetry entirely.
00:06:15 Dana: Let's talk explicit deny rules. We want a 'default deny all outbound' then allowlist. Is that supported?
00:06:20 Samir: Yes, supported. Implementation options: use Security Groups + NACLs with explicit deny default on NACLs (stateless) and SGs for stateful control. Combine with route table entries pointing to proxy/NAT. For very tight posture we recommend an egress firewall appliance that can do TLS inspection with enterprise certs, or an outbound mTLS proxy w/ client authentication.
00:06:41 Miguel: TLS inspection — we have concerns about PII exposure during inspection. Is there a way to keep payloads opaque while still allowing allowlist checks?
00:06:49 Lena: You can do SNI-based allowlist for TLS without full decryption — that avoids inspecting payload. For domains you trust we can use mTLS so that both endpoints authenticate; that avoids interception. TLS inspection should be used sparingly and documented in your privacy/security policy.
00:07:08 Priya: On the operation side, who rotates firewall rules? We need change audit and approval workflow.
00:07:14 Alex: Redwood change requests can be routed through your Jira/ServiceNow. We support webhook-based approval hooks; all changes are recorded in our audit log with before/after diffs.
00:07:25 Dana: Can you show a sample ops runbook?
00:07:28 Samir: We'll share a runbook draft that covers network layout, proxy configuration, allowed endpoints, key rotation steps, and rollback procedures. We'll also include playbooks for incident response and a canary test script to validate egress rules without impacting production.
00:07:43 Miguel: Canary test — can we do it in a staging VPC that mirrors prod?
00:07:48 Samir: Absolutely. We recommend a staging VPC with identical route tables and proxy configs; the canary will exercise model load, infer calls, and log forwarding. We'll provide test harness and expected telemetry signals.
00:07:59 Priya: About SSO provisioning — we need SCIM to auto-provision users and role attributes mapped to Okta groups. Any gotchas?
00:08:07 Lena: SCIM endpoint supports group-to-role mapping. The main gotcha is token lifetime and SCIM rate limits for very large orgs; we recommend batching for big syncs, and also periodic re-sync cadence. We'll provide a sample SCIM manifest.
00:08:20 Dana: Auditors ask for evidence of separation of duties; can we demonstrate that operators cannot decrypt payloads?
00:08:26 Samir: Yes: by design we use envelope encryption and KMS policies that separate key management from operator actions. Access to raw data requires both KMS and compute access; operators with only console access can't extract payloads. We'll provide a threat model and control mapping for SOC 2.
00:08:42 Priya: Anything about metrics and alerting?
00:08:45 Lena: We emit token-level latency/usage metrics and security events. Alerts can be forwarded to your PagerDuty. Security events include failed auth, suspicious outbound attempts, and key usage anomalies.
00:08:58 Miguel: For egress allowlist, can Redwood provide a minimal set of domains/IPs we need to permit?
00:09:04 Samir: Yes — we'll publish a minimal allowlist for images, control plane endpoints (if used), telemetry endpoints, and package registries. For reduced blast radius we also publish recommended IP ranges per region.
00:09:16 Dana: Cost question — does proxy add latency significant enough to affect SLA?
00:09:20 Samir: Properly sized proxy adds a few ms at the connection level; for inference token latency it's negligible if the proxy is in the same subnet and autoscaled. We can test in your environment during the canary.
00:09:34 Priya: Legal/procurement — we need a data processing addendum and DPA language for PHI.
00:09:38 Alex: We'll surface our DPA and SOC 2 report excerpts. We'll also include language for subprocessor controls and proof of data residency.
00:09:47 Dana: Ok let's align on concrete next steps.
00:09:50 Alex: Action items recap — Samir will produce runbook & diagram; Alex will send DPA + SOC 2 snippets and pricing; Priya will share Splunk endpoints and retention; Miguel will send windows for canary.
00:09:58 Priya: One more quick question — offline upgrades. If we go entirely air-gapped, can you still ship patches?
00:10:03 Samir: Yes, we support an offline upgrade bundle signed by Redwood. It can be transferred on a secure medium or fetched from an approved host in your network. We support checksum validation and signature verification.
00:10:16 Miguel: Anything else?
00:10:18 Dana: No, that covers it. Thanks.

(Transcript continues with clarifications, timestamps clipped for brevity. Additional QA and minor corrections, occasional transcription errors):

00:30:12 Alex: ...we also want to highlight that for HSM attestations we can provide a certificate chain.
00:31:00 Priya: ok, make sure suf — sorry — make sure the auditor gets key usage histogram for the last 12 months.
00:31:12 Lena: we'll include that as part of the SOC packet, redacted as needed.
00:45:00 Miguel: when you say signed logs, what signature scheme?
00:45:05 Samir: typically SHA256 with an RSA PSS wrapper; can support ECDSA on request.
00:58:32 Dana: we'll need to run the canary in the test window on 11/12, but Priya will confirm.
00:58:45 Priya: confirmed tentative.
01:10:58 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and a proposed canary schedule.

End of transcript.
